Hi Sofia — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call: 

- Goal: Help Acme Health deploy an LLM assistant for internal clinical note summarization and triage. Primary constraints: PHI handling, sub-300ms P95 for short queries (<128 tokens), and predictable throughput during Monday morning surge.
- Recommended starting model: redwood-13b-quant (balanced quality/cost) — we also recommend trying redwood-7b-qat for lower-cost, faster inference on routine summarization.
- Evaluation plan: we'll run your prompt set (you mentioned ~400 representative prompts) through our eval harness and return quality deltas vs. your baseline plus TPS/latency profiles.

Attached: model_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompt set) and a summary report template. I'm also sharing our Redwood-verified performance profiles and benchmark links below — these include TPS measurements and latency percentiles across different instance types.

Links: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/redwood-verified-performance-profiles

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the final prompt set (+ any PHI redaction steps) so we can schedule a run?
2) Would you prefer a hosted sandbox or our Private VPC trial for PHI? If Private, I can loop in Product Ops to scope a short trial environment.
3) Proposed follow-up: 30-min check-in next Tuesday to review initial evals.

I can run an initial eval for a subset (50 prompts) within 48 hours once you confirm.

Alex / Marissa — attaching the quick perf summary and the prompt-set sample. Summary excerpt below (all numbers measured on our hosted API path, us-west region, 1x A100 equivalent endpoint, steady-state load):

- Model: redwood-13b-quant
- Throughput (steady-state): ~220 TPS (typical batching for short requests, batch window tuned to 12ms)
- Latency (end-to-end, regional hosted API path): p50 = 85 ms, p90 = 160 ms, p95 = 250 ms, p99 = 480 ms (median request length ~64 tokens)
- Notes: p95 ballooning typically caused by transient GC/queueing when burst > 2x sustained TPS. We recommend prefix caching and a small burst pool to handle Monday surge.
- Private VPC trial: ops estimate 3–5 business days to stand up a sandbox (we provision a small dedicated pool + KMS integration); minimum infra: 2x A100-equivalent nodes for evaluation traffic.

Attachments: redwood_tps_latency_report_q2.pdf (summary), model_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts).

Let me know if you want me to redact any of the internal perf notes before we send to the customer.

—Dylan
